title: Sell Mineral Rights in Morrisville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Morrisville, PA | Greene County
metaDescription: Morrisville, PA sits in Greene County's core Marcellus wet-gas window. We buy mineral and royalty interests directly, no broker, no waiting around.
heroLead: Morrisville is a small Greene County community where family farms and Marcellus drilling units have become so intertwined that a lot of local landowners can name the well pad nearest their property from memory.
intro: Greene County has been one of the most heavily developed counties in the entire Marcellus play, and Morrisville, tucked into the county's rural southwest, has been part of that story from early on. If your family's land is anywhere near here, chances are it's connected to a unit, whether through your own lease or through inheritance from a relative who signed one years ago.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Morrisville directly. We'll research your title, review your production history, and give you a clear offer without shopping your interest around to anyone else.

sections.heading: Deep in Greene County's Core
paragraphs: Operators have run extensive multi-well pad development throughout southwestern Greene County for well over a decade, and Morrisville sits right in the middle of that activity. Wet-gas production here means liquids revenue is part of the value equation, along with the processing deductions that come with it.

If your family's tract has been part of more than one unit over the years as operators expanded their acreage position, that's common in this part of the county and doesn't complicate a sale beyond needing more careful title research.

sections.heading: Rural Title Research, Done Right
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Greene County Recorder of Deeds in Waynesburg, working through older farm-boundary language where necessary to confirm exactly what your family's interest covers today.
Greene County's rural parcels sometimes carry deed language from before modern surveying, and we take the time to reconcile that against current unit maps.

sections.heading: Act 13 Impact Fees and Your Royalty
paragraphs: Greene County has received substantial Act 13 impact fee revenue over the years, funding local infrastructure and services. That's separate from what you're paid as a mineral owner, and we always keep those two things distinct when explaining your specific interest's value.

faqs.question: My land near Morrisville has been part of multiple units. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No, it's common in heavily developed parts of Greene County. We just need to trace the full history to give you an accurate offer.

faqs.question: Does the county receiving impact fee money affect my royalty?
faqs.answer: No, Act 13 impact fees are a separate county-level payment unrelated to your personal royalty, which is governed by your specific lease and division order.

faqs.question: What if my deed uses old-style farm boundary descriptions?
faqs.answer: That's common in rural Greene County and something we regularly work through as part of our title research at no cost to you.
